title: Auto-mask run cost + feedback - cache per-object masks, then queue what is left
description:
Auto-mask detection (Detect / Points / Text) dispatches a real ComfyUI workflow but is invisible while it runs. `runAutoMask` (js/services/commandExecutor.js:876), called from `_runAutoMaskWorkflow` (js/components/Organisms/MpiCanvasViewer/MpiCanvasViewer.js:479), returns an `AutoMaskExecution` handle whose contract is onDetected / onMasks / onError / cancel -- there is NO onProgress, where the `Execution` typedef immediately below it in the same file has one. So a detect run never enters the queue and never reaches the StatusBar progress bar that generations use (js/services/generationService.js, generationStore.js, activeGenerations.js). CONSEQUENCE: a pass over a busy image -- many objects, or SAM3 text with several categories -- can take a long time with zero feedback. The user cannot tell it from a hang, and has no visible way to stop it even though the handle already exposes cancel(). These are ComfyUI workflows like any other, so they belong in the same lane. DECIDE: do they occupy the queue as first-class jobs, or a lightweight utility lane that cannot end up stuck behind a long generation? Read docs/generation-lifecycle.md and docs/masking-sam3.md before touching this. Raised by the user 2026-07-31.

MERGED 2026-08-01: this card absorbs MPI-402 (Auto-mask chip toggling re-runs the whole workflow - cache per-object masks client-side).
- MPI-402 - every chip select re-dispatches the full graph; only deselect-to-zero is client-side.
WHY ONE CARD: Both cards live in the same call path - _runAutoMaskWorkflow in MpiCanvasViewer.js and runAutoMask in commandExecutor.js. MPI-402 removes most of the dispatches; this card gives the ones that survive a queue lane, a progress signal and a Stop. Do them together or the progress work gets written for runs that should not happen at all. NOT merged and still separate: MPI-403 (engineAssets never staged to the Pod fast disk) is the download/staging subsystem, even though it also makes the first Detect slow.
The absorbed card(s) are closed as done/rejected - not built, kept as the record - and their full original text stays on disk at tasks/<id>/.

--- NOTE 2026-08-01, MPI-424 brainstorm ---
Unchanged in substance, but the surface shrinks: after MPI-425 the three detect engines sit behind ONE Detect button (a floating strip picks points / text / auto), so this card instruments and caches ONE panel's dispatch path rather than three. It is independent of the rest of the umbrella and can be picked up at any point.
